en: The Therāpadāna, Chattavagga 9. The Apadāna of the Elder Vaṭaṃsakiya In the past, when the lifespan of beings was twenty thousand years, there appeared in the world the Blessed One Kassapa, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. At that time, I was a young man, a master of the three Vedas, skilled in the interpretation of signs and omens. Seeing the Blessed One Kassapa, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, I thought: "I shall offer a parasol to this Blessed One. Having obtained a parasol made of cloth, I offered it to the Blessed One. Because of that deed, for ninety-one eons I did not fall into the states of misery; rather, I was reborn in the heavenly realms. When the Blessed One Gotama, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, appeared in the world, I was reborn as a human being. Now, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I have realized the fruit of stream-entry. This is my final birth; there will be no further existence for me. This is the apadāna of the Elder Vaṭaṃsakiya.
“Named Sumedha, the self-arisen and unconquered, cultivating solitude, The name of the one who is self-arisen and unconquered is Sumedha;
he cultivates seclusion.
Plunged deep into the great forest;
seeing a flowering salala tree,
she plucked its blossoms and fashioned them into a garland.
I offered it to the Buddha,
in the presence of the Leader of the World.
Thirty thousand aeons ago,
Because I offered that flower,
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
In the one hundred and nineteen eons [prior],
there were sixteen Sunimmita kings,
endowed with the seven treasures.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
"Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Vaṭaṃsakiya recited these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Vaṭaṃsakiya.
